pattern.crimePattern: a former court clerk forges a codicil in her husband's favour and kills the elderly testator with a lit charcoal stove in a sealed bedroom, to look like an accident
pattern.notes: Fictional family, advocates and registry. Jiko deaths in closed rooms are a known highland tragedy; the case never shows the death, only the room. Forgery flaws only, never method.

ob.text: A farm worker, back from his day off, reports an elderly widow, Wambui Githinji (74), found dead in her bedroom on her tea farm near Othaya. A burned-out charcoal stove was in the room, the door and window shut. Suspected carbon-monoxide accident.

facts.text: Wambui Githinji was found dead in her bedroom on Monday morning, a burned-out charcoal stove in the room, door and window shut.
She lay in bed, covered, with no injuries; a burned-out jiko by the bed.
The jiko in the bedroom has one leg repaired with twisted wire.
The bedroom window is latched from inside, its gap stuffed with a cloth.
Wambui's Bible: a ribbon bookmark at the Psalms, and no fold marks anywhere. The codicil is folded in four.
Tea-factory share certificate: Wambui Githinji, numbered and signed by the factory.
Title for the six acres: Wambui Githinji, registered in 1987.
Kitchen hut: her two jikos both stand there, neither with a wired leg. A pot of porridge, half eaten.
Mama Wanjiku: Ndinda's car stood at Wambui's gate on Saturday evening; she heard it leave at about 23:00.
Mama Wanjiku: Waweru came on Sunday afternoon, about three, shouted at the closed door about the will, and drove off.
Kiragu: "Mama never let a jiko into the house. Never. Her sister died that way in 1990. She cooked in the hut and carried hot water in."
Kiragu was in the workers' house playing draughts with two other workers until midnight on Saturday.
Kiragu: Mama paid the workers every Friday. She paid on Friday; he has the note.
Wambui's will, February: land in four equal shares; the house and tea-factory shares to Muthoni "who nursed me".
Advocate Gakii: "She signed in front of me. Waweru can shout as much as he likes; that will is hers."
Advocate Gakii: Ndinda worked twenty years as a clerk at the Nyeri law courts. "She knows what papers look like."
"Codicil", dated 3 March, typed: the tea-factory shares to Thuo Githinji. Witnesses "Samuel Kiruthi" and "Lucy Wangeci". Lodged by Thuo's advocate on Monday afternoon.
Othaya death register: Samuel Kiruthi died on 9 February 2024, two years before the codicil's date.
Hospital roster: Muthoni on night shift from Saturday 19:00 to Sunday 07:00, signed in and out.
Muthoni: Ndinda's car was at the gate when she left for her shift at 18:30; Ndinda had brought porridge, and the two of them were laughing over it.
Waweru's wife: he was home in Othaya town from 19:00 on Saturday and didn't go out.
Thuo's neighbour: he watched the football at Thuo's house in Karatina from 20:30 to 23:30 on Saturday; Ndinda was out.
Records, Ndinda's line: Othaya farms zone, Saturday 18:20–23:05.
Ndinda's kitchen: two jikos of a set of three, their legs repaired with the same twisted wire as the jiko in Wambui's bedroom.
In Ndinda's drawer: a sheet with Wambui's signature written over and over in pencil.
Autopsy: carbon-monoxide poisoning.
Autopsy: death between 01:00 and 04:00 on Sunday.
Autopsy: no injuries, no signs of smothering, a sound heart.
Autopsy: no poison or drug in her blood or stomach.
Under the raking light: the codicil's signature has a faint pencil line beneath the ink, traced over. It is ink, not a photocopy.
The codicil carries no stamp of any kind: no advocate's stamp, no printed seal.
Wilfrida Ayugi: forged. The signature is traced from the February will; the codicil is typed on a printer, while Wambui wrote her own papers by hand.
Wilfrida Ayugi: the pencil practice sheet and the codicil signature. "The same hand practised it."
Ndinda: "I left Mama's house at eight on Saturday and drove home."
Ndinda: "Thuo found the codicil in her Bible."
Ndinda: she stayed to help Wambui to bed, at about half past ten, and left when she slept.
Ndinda: "I lit nothing. I carried nothing into that room."
Ndinda: "I have never written that woman's name in my life."
Thuo: "I found the codicil in Mama's Bible on Monday."
Thuo: Ndinda "found" it and gave it to him, and told him to say he found it. He didn't ask.
Waweru: "That will is forged."
Waweru: "I haven't been to Mother's house since Easter."
Waweru: he went on Sunday afternoon to shout at her about the will and shouted at a closed door. "She'd been dead since the morning. I didn't know."
Muthoni: "I was on night shift."

interrogations.intro: Ndinda pours tea before you ask. "I left Mama's house at eight on Saturday and drove home. And Thuo found the codicil in her Bible, God rest her."

topics.reply: "Muthoni nursed her. Nobody denies that. But Thuo was like a son."

lawyered.line: On my advocate's advice, no comment.

interrogations.intro: Thuo sits beside Advocate Muchiri with his hands flat on his knees. "On my advocate's advice, no comment."
Waweru stands in the yard with his arms folded. "That will is forged. And I haven't been to Mother's house since Easter."
Muthoni sits on the step of the kitchen hut in her coat. "I was on night shift."
Kiragu holds his hat in both hands. "Mama never let a jiko into the house. Never."
Advocate Gakii unties the pink tape on Wambui's file.

contradictions.reaction: She sets the teapot down carefully. "I stayed to help her to bed. I lit nothing. I left when she slept."
Ndinda looks at the death register entry and says nothing for the first time.
"Ndinda found it. She gave it to me and told me to say I found it. I didn't ask." Advocate Muchiri, to Amani: "He's telling you the truth now. Don't waste it."
The shouting goes out of him. "I went on Sunday to shout at her about the will. She'd been dead since the morning. I didn't know. I shouted at a closed door and left."
Ndinda looks at the two wired jikos from her own kitchen, photographed side by side with the third.
"I was a clerk for twenty years," she says. "I know how a signature should look." Then she asks for a lawyer.

timeOfDeath.note: The act window: the lit jiko went in after Wambui fell asleep at about 22:30 and before Ndinda's car left at 23:00. She died of it between 01:00 and 04:00.

reconstruction.text: February. Wambui makes her will with Advocate Gakii: land in four shares, the house and tea-factory shares to Muthoni, who nursed her. Waweru tells everyone it's forged. It isn't.

Ndinda, twenty years a court clerk, types a "codicil" leaving the shares to her husband, traces Wambui's signature from a copy of the will, and invents two witnesses. One of the names she chooses belongs to a man who died in 2024.
Saturday, 18:30. Ndinda brings porridge. They laugh over it. Muthoni leaves for her night shift.
About 22:30 Wambui falls asleep. Ndinda carries a lit jiko from her own kitchen set into the bedroom, closes the door, latches the window and stuffs its gap with a cloth.
23:00. Her car leaves. On Sunday afternoon Waweru shouts at a closed door. On Monday Thuo's advocate lodges a codicil "found in her Bible".

clockPlan.note: Two stamps: records on Ndinda and a warrant on her kitchen. Thuo stays silent until the death register is put in front of him. The codicil goes to the Questioned Documents Lab from the advocate's office; the handwriting comparison follows the warrant.

ui.beatNotes: Lawyered-up suspects. Thuo's statement sheet is stamped "NO COMMENT — ADV. B. MUCHIRI" until the player drags the death-register entry onto it; Muchiri leans in and says "Thuo, answer." The FORGERY group accepts either proven tell (the dead witness, or the traced signature).
